# Fig Performance

> Private one-on-one personal training gym in Placentia, California, for adults over 40 who want to lose fat, build muscle and get stronger. Coached by Daniel Figueroa ("Coach Dan"), an ACSM certified personal trainer and Precision Nutrition Level 1 certified nutrition coach. Progress is measured with InBody body-composition scans, and semi-private clients get red light and vibration therapy for recovery.

- Address: 1284 E. Yorba Linda Blvd, Placentia, CA 92870
- Phone: (714) 396-7178
- Email: trainat@figperformance.com
- Staffed hours: Monday to Friday 5 AM to 8:30 PM, Saturday 5 AM to 12 PM, closed Sunday. Personal training is by appointment.
- Serves: Placentia, Yorba Linda, Brea, Fullerton, Anaheim Hills and Villa Park (Orange County, CA)
- Reviews: 74 reviews of Coach Dan in total (checked Nov 24, 2026): 5.0 on Google with 23 reviews of Fig Performance, 5.0 on Yelp with 39 reviews (that page is now named FIG PERFORMANCE at 1284 E. Yorba Linda Blvd, Placentia; the reviews were earned under the business's former name, Train With Dan) and 12 more five-star reviews from people Dan coached before opening Fig Performance
- Price: two ways to train. One-on-one personal training is $60 to $90 a session, billed weekly or monthly, with a 3-month minimum; the exact rate depends on how often you train, and it is given in writing at the free consult. Semi-private small-group training starts at $180/month (1x a week), then $225 (2x), $279 (3x) or $345 (4x), with red light and vibration therapy included (3-month minimum, pause anytime). There is no membership or open gym option. No initiation fee. The first consult is free. Book it online: https://www.figperformance.com/#consult

## Guides for adults over 40

- [Fitness after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/fitness-after-40): index of all guides
- [Body composition terms explained](https://www.figperformance.com/body-composition-glossary): plain definitions of every number on an InBody printout (body fat percentage, fat mass, skeletal muscle mass, lean mass by segment, visceral fat level, body water, BMR) plus body recomposition, sarcopenia, progressive overload, red light therapy and whole body vibration
- [What is personal training for adults over 40](https://www.figperformance.com/what-is-personal-training-for-adults-over-40): plain definition of the service and what a good program includes
- [Strength training after 50](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-after-50): what it is, why it matters, whether it is safe
- [What is private personal training](https://www.figperformance.com/what-is-private-personal-training): private one-on-one vs big-box, semi-private and online
- [Strength training for weight loss](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-weight-loss): why lifting beats cardio alone for fat loss
- [Simple meal plan for weight loss + grocery list (free PDF)](https://www.figperformance.com/meal-plan-for-weight-loss): protein, carbs, fats and fiber at every meal; palm of protein, fist of vegetables, high-fiber carbs; breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack options; free PDF at https://www.figperformance.com/assets/fig-performance-meal-plan.pdf
- [How to lose 10 pounds in a month](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-lose-10-pounds-in-a-month): realistic with about a 1,000-calorie daily deficit (500 food, 500 movement), high protein and strength training; about 8 lb fat plus water; client Adriana, 48, lost 10 lb in her first month
- [Dumbbell workout for beginners over 50](https://www.figperformance.com/dumbbell-workout-for-beginners-over-50): dumbbells and an adjustable bench, 2-3 days a week (full body every other day, full body 2x, or upper/lower); exercise menu by muscle; RPE 1-10 explained as reps left in the tank, aim 7-9; +2 reps or +5 lb a week when ready; shoulder, knee and back swaps; Sam, 70, started with dumbbells (15 reps, then 5, then 6-10) and now deadlifts 135 lb
- [Calorie deficit after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/calorie-deficit): weight loss is thermodynamics (Haub 2010 Twinkie diet: 27 lb in 10 weeks at 1,800 kcal/day, LDL -20%, HDL +20%); Coach Dan sets deficits from InBody BMR plus activity and job, usually 300-500 kcal/day, one-to-two-week test, weekly InBody; up to 1,000 kcal short-term only; plans built from foods clients already eat, more protein and fiber, 80/20; three new-year rules: get a coach, get a plan, do it
- [Hotel workout](https://www.figperformance.com/hotel-workout): Coach Dan trains on the road in any country by finding a gym nearby and buying a day or week pass (dumbbells, bench, cables; pull-up bar a bonus); 1-2 sessions a week keeps the routine; reps 12-25 with light dumbbells, 6-12 with heavier; room-only fallback circuit; pack gym clothes only; stock up on protein shakes, bars and snacks on arrival; protein floor on the road 100 g/day men, 80 g women (two shakes, a bar or Greek yogurt, dinner with protein and fiber); holiday travel: walk daily, pick drinking nights, book the first session back
- [Building muscle after 50](https://www.figperformance.com/building-muscle-after-50): realistic gains (Peterson 2011: ~2.4 lb lean mass in 20 weeks on average; ~1 lb/month early for people who never trained hard); recovery takes longer after 50 (2-3 lifting days, never back to back, 7+ h sleep); protein at goal weight in grams (PROT-AGE floor 1.2 g/kg if active); creatine monohydrate 5-10 g/day, safe for healthy adults (Antonio 2021, ISSN 2017), benefits for older adults and possibly memory
- [Strength training for women over 60](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-women-over-60): same formula as everyone, different starting point; heavy lifting for bone (LIFTMOR 2018: +2.9% spine BMD); balance = isometrics, eccentrics, unilateral leg work (Cochrane 2019: exercise cuts falls 23%, with strength ~34%); protein at goal weight in grams (PROT-AGE floor 1.0-1.2 g/kg), fiber 22 g+ for women 51+; Teresa 60: first pull-up in ~3 months, benches ~85 lb; Danielle: isometrics and unilateral work after a car accident left her tripping
- [Is belly fat the last to go?](https://www.figperformance.com/is-belly-fat-the-last-to-go): yes, the lower belly; the body stores reserves around the organs; visceral fat is lost first (Chaston 2008), lower-abdominal fat cells resist lipolysis (Wahrenberg 1989); cortisol and central fat (Epel 2000); InBody visceral fat target under 6; crunches don't burn fat (Vispute 2011) but weighted core work builds definition; walk 30 min daily, lift 2x/week, goal-weight protein; Priscilla, over 42, lost 20 lb and flattened her stomach in 2-3 months
- [Hip thrust form and why women over 40 need it](https://www.figperformance.com/hip-thrust): setup (bench 12-24 in, bar at hip crease with thick pad, knees at 90 degrees), full hip extension, power up, squeeze throughout; 3 leg days a week with hip thrust + squat + hinge + abduction, ~32 leg sets a week (Bret Contreras seminar, Aug 2026); client went 55 lb to 135 lb in six weeks
- [Are Jefferson curls safe?](https://www.figperformance.com/jefferson-curls): Coach Dan Jefferson curls 205 lb; loaded spinal flexion trains the range daily life uses; start at body weight to a bench, add range then 2.5 lb steps, 1-8 slow reps; cautions for osteoporosis and disc injury; Jonathan, 43, from back pain to 135 lb
- [Strength training for seniors](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-seniors): Coach Dan's approach for adults 65+: assess, then train push, pull, squat, hinge, carry and overhead; 8-10 reps then lower reps and heavier weight; add 2 reps or 2.5-5 lb a week; client results (Randy 73 benches 135 with shoulder arthritis)
- [How to lose belly fat after menopause](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-lose-belly-fat-after-menopause): research-backed plan for women after menopause: strength training with progressive overload 2-3x a week, a small calorie deficit with whole fiber-rich foods, at least 1.2 g/kg protein, creatine 5 g a day, daily walking, sleep, and asking a doctor about hormone therapy
- [GLP-1s and muscle loss](https://www.figperformance.com/glp-1-muscle-loss): how to keep muscle on semaglutide or tirzepatide: protein at least goal weight in grams, lifting 2-3x a week, enough calories, daily walking, and habits for after stopping
- [Strength training for women over 50](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-women-over-50): age doesn't decide the program, the assessment does; menopause, bone density (LIFTMOR), protein; clients Teresa (60) and Sam (70)
- [Workout plan for men over 40](https://www.figperformance.com/workout-plan-for-men-over-40): train for function, start light, fix neck, shoulders, back, hips and knees; client Jonathan, 43, went from back pain to a 185 lb bench
- [Tib raises](https://www.figperformance.com/tib-raises): why the tibialis anterior matters for shock absorption, knees and shin splints; wall tib raises, kettlebell toe raises, tib bar; 5-30 reps
- [3-day workout split for beginners](https://www.figperformance.com/3-day-beginner-workout-plan): why full body 3 days a week works, and links to the women's and men's plans
- [Beginner workout plan for women](https://www.figperformance.com/beginner-workout-plan-for-women): Coach Dan's 3-day full-body plan: 4 leg and glute exercises (squat or lunge, hinge, hip thrust, abduction last), 2 upper body, 1 core (2 sets) a day, rest 1:15-2 min, warm-up, exercise guide with easier and at-home versions
- [Beginner workout plan for men](https://www.figperformance.com/beginner-workout-plan-for-men): Coach Dan's 3-day split: 2 leg exercises and 1 calf exercise first each day, chest/back/shoulders on days 1 and 3, arm day in the middle, wall tib raises, 2 core sets, rest 1:15-2 min
- [How to avoid holiday weight gain after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-avoid-holiday-weight-gain): Coach Dan's rules: protein first, room for dessert (he eats 80/20), train on Thanksgiving, set drink boundaries, keep each holiday to a few days, plus a hotel workout
- [How to lose weight after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-lose-weight-after-40): Coach Dan's plan for busy professionals: daily steps, protein, lifting heavy enough, training twice a week, hormones, and body recomposition
- [Can you build muscle after 60?](https://www.figperformance.com/build-muscle-after-60): yes, with two client examples (Teresa, 60, first pull-up in about 3 months; Sam, 70, deadlifting 135 lb for reps) and the exact progression used
- [Why am I not losing weight?](https://www.figperformance.com/why-am-i-not-losing-weight): Coach Dan says you're almost always not in a true calorie deficit; nine reasons (portions, protein at 0.7-1 g per lb, progressive overload, daily steps, sleep, stress, measuring, medical) and what to do about each
- [Strength training for women over 40](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-women-over-40): how often to lift, what to do, how heavy, and a sample week

- [How much protein after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/how-much-protein-after-40): the RDA of 0.8 g/kg is a floor, not a target; PROT-AGE recommends 1.0-1.2 g/kg a day for adults over 65 and more for those training; anabolic resistance means older adults need more protein per meal; aim for 25-35 g at each main meal
- [Strength training for bone density after 50](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-bone-density): walking and swimming do not load bone enough to build it; the LIFTMOR trial put 101 postmenopausal women with low bone mass through 30-minute supervised sessions twice a week for 8 months (deadlift, back squat, overhead press, jumping chin-up) and improved spine and hip bone mineral density safely
- [In-N-Out after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/in-n-out-after-40): a Double-Double is about 610 calories and 34 g protein; regular fries about 360 calories and 6 g; Protein Style saves roughly 150 calories and 30 g carbs without changing the protein
- [Chipotle after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/chipotle-after-40): adobo chicken is 180 calories for 32 g protein, the best ratio on the menu; the official Double High Protein Bowl is 81 g for 760 calories; calories hide in the toppings, not the protein
- [Chick-fil-A after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/chick-fil-a-after-40): 8-count grilled nuggets are 130 calories, 25 g protein and 440 mg sodium against 250 calories and 1,210 mg for breaded; the grilled and fried sandwiches are 30 calories apart
- [El Pollo Loco after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/el-pollo-loco-after-40): a fire-grilled chicken breast is 200 calories and 34 g protein; the Mexican Caesar Salad is about 52 g for 350 calories; the bowls carry 2,030 to 2,670 mg of sodium
- [Starbucks after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/starbucks-after-40): protein cold foam adds about 15 g protein for 80 calories; an iced vanilla protein latte is about 29 g for 270 calories; egg bites run 150 to 300 calories with 12 to 19 g
- [Raising Cane's after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/raising-canes-after-40): three chicken fingers alone are about 390 calories and 39 g protein, while one Cane's Sauce is about 190 calories and 18 g fat, more than a 130-calorie finger; the 3 Finger Combo is around 1,050 calories
- [Jersey Mike's after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/jersey-mikes-after-40): ordering any sub as a "sub in a tub" removes the bread and cuts roughly 250 to 350 calories and about 50 g carbs with the protein unchanged; Mike's Way oil adds about 100 calories; a Regular sub can carry up to about 3,530 mg sodium
- [Panera after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/panera-after-40): the sourdough bread bowl alone is roughly 570 to 650 calories, more than the about 420-calorie bowl of broccoli cheddar soup inside it; the two together reach about 890 to 950 calories and roughly 2,170 mg sodium
- [KFC after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/kfc-after-40): an Original Recipe breast is 390 calories, 39 g protein and 1,190 mg sodium; Extra Crispy adds about 140 calories and 14 g fat for the same cut; the Kentucky Grilled breast is about 210 calories and 38 g protein where stores still carry it
- [Del Taco after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/del-taco-after-40): from Del Taco's own November 2026 nutritional list, a Grilled Chicken Street Taco is 110 calories, 9 g protein and 300 mg sodium, so three come to 330 calories and 27 g protein, beating the Taco Salad with Fresh Guac (420 cal, 26 g, 1,270 mg) on calories, protein and sodium; the Epic Loaded Queso burritos run 2,770 to 3,130 mg sodium
- [WaBa Grill after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/waba-grill-after-40): asking for white meat gives about 46 g protein for roughly 630 calories against about 38 g for 640 in the regular Chicken Bowl, so eight more grams at slightly fewer calories; the White Meat Chicken Veggie Bowl is near 580 cal and 47 g; published sodium figures for this chain disagree from about 900 to 2,455 mg so the page declines to state one
- [Flame Broiler after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/flame-broiler-after-40): a full chicken bowl with white rice is about 600 calories with roughly 45 g protein and only around 340 mg sodium, the lowest of any full meal in these guides; the sauce roughly triples the salt so ask for it on the side; note that database entries showing 250-270 calories are the protein portion only, not a bowl with rice
- [Five Guys after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/five-guys-after-40): a bunless hamburger is about 440 calories with roughly 32 g protein and only around 100 mg sodium, and a bunless Little Hamburger is about 220 cal with 16 g; the bun is worth about 240 calories and Five Guys will serve any sandwich as a bowl or lettuce wrap; Little means one patty not a small burger; burgers run only 380-430 mg sodium, far below most chains
- [Jack in the Box after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/jack-in-the-box-after-40): grilled chicken strips (4 pc) are about 200 calories with roughly 30 g protein, the best item on the menu; the Grilled Chicken Salad is about 320 cal and 32 g; choosing grilled over crispy saves roughly 150-200 calories; published sodium figures for this chain disagree from about 900 to 1,440 mg for the same sandwich so the page declines to state one
- [Popeyes after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/popeyes-after-40): five Blackened Tenders are about 280 calories with roughly 47 g protein, the best protein-per-calorie order in any of these guides; three are about 170 cal with 26-28 g; the Classic or Spicy Chicken Sandwich is about 700 cal with 28 g protein and 1,440 mg sodium, so the tenders give 19 more grams of protein for 420 fewer calories; three classic breaded tenders carry about 1,820 mg sodium against 550-860 for blackened
- [CAVA after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/cava-after-40): CAVA's curated (pre-designed) bowls run about 1,670-2,210 mg sodium each against a 2,300 mg daily value, while a bowl built on a greens base with grilled chicken, hummus and tzatziki is about 395 calories with roughly 37 g protein and around 1,045 mg sodium; grilled chicken is 250 cal / 28 g / 670 mg; grilled steak carries about 390 mg LESS sodium than the chicken; falafel is about 350 cal for only 6 g protein
- [Carl's Jr after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/carls-jr-after-40): at the same 440 calories, five Hand-Breaded Chicken Tenders give about 41 g protein while the Charbroiled BBQ Chicken Sandwich gives about 35 g, so the breaded item wins on protein per calorie here, the opposite of KFC and Chick-fil-A, because the sandwich carries a bun and BBQ sauce worth 48-57 g carbs; the sandwich's 440 calorie figure comes from Carl's Jr's own menu page; sodium in it runs about 1,310-1,350 mg
- [Dunkin after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/dunkin-after-40): the Wake-Up Wrap is about 180 calories with only 7-8 g protein, making it a snack rather than a breakfast; the Egg White and Veggie Omelet Bites are the best item at about 180 cal and 13 g protein; this is the lowest protein restaurant in the series, and Starbucks now beats it for a protein stop because its protein lattes carry close to 29 g
- [Wingstop after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/wingstop-after-40): a classic bone-in wing is about 90-120 calories with 10 g protein regardless of flavour, so six plain are about 540 cal and 60 g; the FLAVOUR is the real variable because a Plain wing carries about 30 mg sodium and a Cajun wing about 310 mg for identical calories and protein, a tenfold swing; classic bone-in carries roughly twice the protein of boneless, which are breaded
- [The Habit after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/habit-burger-after-40): a Lettuce Wrap Charburger is about 290 calories with roughly 18 g protein and around 840 mg sodium, against 470 cal on the seeded bun or 520 on wheat with 1,140-1,220 mg; sodium is the real issue at this chain, with most burgers clearing 1,000 mg and the BBQ Bacon at about 1,760 mg and Teriyaki at about 1,690 mg; the Double Charburger is about 730 cal and 37 g protein
- [Rubio's after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/rubios-after-40): The Original Fish Taco is about 330 calories for only 9 g protein because it is battered and fried, while the Grilled Gourmet Chicken Taco is the SAME 330 calories for about 20 g; the grilled tacos are the real menu, with a Grilled Atlantic Salmon taco at about 270 cal, 13 g protein and only around 160 mg sodium, among the lowest of any item in these guides; the Coastal Trio is about 850 cal and 1,250 mg sodium
- [McDonald's after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/mcdonalds-after-40): the McDouble is 390 calories with 22 g protein, 20 g fat and 920 mg sodium, giving 5.6 g protein per 100 calories against about 4.3 for a Big Mac at roughly 580 cal and 25 g, so the McDouble wins on ratio and costs less; the Egg McMuffin is the breakfast pick at 310 cal, 17 g protein, 770 mg sodium; the Big Breakfast is about 1,060 cal and the hotcakes version about 1,340 with 41 g added sugar
- [Taco Bell after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/taco-bell-after-40): three Soft Chicken Tacos are about 480 calories with roughly 36 g protein, beating the Chicken Power Menu Bowl at about 470 cal and 26-27 g despite the bowl being branded as the performance item; ordering the bowl without rice brings it near 360 cal while keeping about 25 g; Fresco style is a free modification that swaps cheese and creamy sauces for pico de gallo; the Power Bowl carries about 1,230 mg sodium
- [Wendy's after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/wendys-after-40): a small chili is about 240-280 calories with roughly 15-17 g protein, which makes it almost unique among fast food sides where fries deliver 4-6 g for more calories; a Grilled Chicken Sandwich is about 350-370 cal with 33-35 g protein and 810-880 mg sodium, so sandwich plus small chili is about 610 cal and 51 g protein; a Baconator is about 960 cal, 57 g protein and 1,960 mg sodium
- [Subway after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/subway-after-40): Subway serves any sub as a No Bready Bowl, a named menu format, and rotisserie chicken that way is about 220 calories with roughly 31 g protein against 600-700 calories for the same filling in a footlong; the sodium spread between protein bowls is enormous, roughly 950 mg for grilled chicken against about 2,540 mg for spicy Italian; Subway's published figures are less consistent than most chains so this page gives ranges
- [Panda Express after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/panda-express-after-40): a Super Greens base with Teriyaki Chicken is about 470 calories with roughly 50 g protein, while Chow Mein with Orange Chicken and Beijing Beef is about 1,580 calories and 2,450 mg sodium; Grilled Teriyaki Chicken is the best entree at about 275-280 cal with 33-38 g protein and 470-630 mg sodium, against Orange Chicken at about 490-510 cal for only 25-26 g; the base you choose decides the meal
## Client case studies

- [Client case studies](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies): index of all fifteen, fat loss, strength and training around pain, studio and online
- [Jonathan, 43](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/jonathan): ex-Army, a new son, a stiff and achy back and a sore shoulder; had quit golf. Pull-ups 1 to 5, chin-ups with +35 lb, Jefferson curl 135 lb, bench 185 lb, and back on the golf course. Studio
- [Rosa, 43](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/rosa): 205 to 169 lb in 11 months. Long shifts, home hungry with dinner undecided; had tried cutting carbs, shakes and a boot camp. Two studio times she could usually make plus a few dinners she could grab on the way home. Studio
- [Ray, 64](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/ray): 218 to 183 lb in 10 months. Walked mornings, did yard work, had not lifted in years and had started asking for help carrying things. Lifting twice a week, morning walks kept. Studio
- [Chris, 50](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/chris): 224 to 193 lb in 9 months. Trained well at home, lost the routine on work trips. A home lifting plan plus a short dumbbell workout for hotel days and a few reliable restaurant orders. Online
- [Matt, 39](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/matt): 212 to 184 lb in 7 months. Lifted in his twenties, then work and kids; a 30-day challenge and strict meal prep both failed when his schedule moved. Two sessions he could usually make and a shorter workout for busy weeks. Studio
- [Jenna, 34](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/jenna): 172 to 154 lb in 6 months. Had a gym membership but used the treadmill and the same machines; uncomfortable learning a new lift in a busy weight room. Learned to set up lifts, choose a starting weight and progress. Studio
- [Linda, 57](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/linda): 149 to 143 lb in 6 months. Walked with friends and rarely missed a class, but had used the same dumbbells for years. Kept what she enjoyed and added tracked lifts. Studio
- [Eric, 52](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/eric): 181 to 176 lb in 8 months. Ran and lifted when he could; added sets, swapped exercises from videos and tried a six-day split, but work trips broke the rhythm. A shorter plan with the same key lifts logged weekly. Online
- [Natalie, 38](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/natalie): 137 to 134 lb in 7 months. Pilates, weekend runs and occasional lifting; wanted definition, and more cardio with smaller portions left her flat. Regular lifting, tracked. Three pounds on the scale, a visible change in shoulders and legs. Online
- [Greg, 55](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/greg): 232 to 205 lb in 8 months. Regional sales leader. Weekday workouts vanished with every trip. Studio
- [Lauren, 42](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/lauren): 151 to 144 lb in 5 months. CFO. Lifting was the first thing to go every month-end close. Online
- [Diane, 58](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/diane): 148 to 139 lb in 7 months. Chiropractor, on her feet all day. The after-work workout rarely happened. Studio
- [Marcus, 47](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/marcus): 218 to 196 lb in 7 months. Cybersecurity IT manager. A late incident could take the whole evening. Studio
- [Alyssa, 36](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/alyssa): 167 to 149 lb in 6 months. CEO living on flights and late client dinners. Online
- [Karen, 53](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/karen): 176 to 152 lb in 9 months. Enterprise sales leader. Strength training kept waiting for next quarter. Studio
